item.title: quant-investment-platform — mid-retrospective
item.description: A mid-project retrospective on a personal automated trading platform built with Rust + Python + React. With ETF rebalancing and single-stock signal trading both in place, a record of how the safety layers — halt, block, detect, simulate — got built before going live.

item.title: I Threw Away My AirPods
item.description: A good engineer isn’t someone who knows technology well, but someone who can share that knowledge with their team.

item.title: LR-based ML Lifecycle Retrospective
item.description: Building my first ML Lifecycle — a three-tier architecture for an ad Fallback CTR prediction — as a backend engineer without an AI background. The technical decisions I made, and what I learned through running it.

item.title: Sensitive Data Encryption — Module Design and Migration Retrospective
item.description: A retrospective on column-level encryption of sensitive data in a running service. Envelope encryption, DEK granularity decisions, the WHERE clause constraint that led to HMAC, and the migration automation Skill that spread the work across the org.

item.title: Internal Hackathon Retrospective — 1st Place
item.description: A retrospective on the internal hackathon. How an idea I proposed evolved with the team into a 1st-place project and an internal launch — and the starting point for using AI tools in earnest.

item.title: Profitability-Based Traffic Throttling Retrospective
item.description: Retrospective on building a system that automatically identifies low-performing SSP inventory and throttles traffic to improve contribution margin. Covers the evolution from Imp Cost Ratio to a predicted contribution margin rate approach.

item.title: Ad System Outage Retrospective — A Shared Dependency and a Single Point of Failure
item.description: An external event drove ad traffic far above normal, triggering a cascading failure. The real problem was that the filtering component was a single point of failure — and the fallback sat on top of it too, so one collapse pulled both down at once. The fix took three paths: removing the fallback’s dependency (independence), adding rate limiting to the component itself (protection), and reconsidering the runtime (throughput).

item.title: The Blind Spot in Deploy Change Verification — Campaign Cache Incident Retrospective
item.description: The deploy was two days old, and the metrics had been calm the whole time. The moment we turned off the cache refresh batch, ad serving stopped. A retrospective on the missing verification of what a deploy actually changed.

item.title: concurrency-go
item.description: A record of implementing and benchmarking three Go concurrency patterns — mutex, channel, and lock-free — to build hands-on understanding.

item.title: chat-services
item.description: A record of designing and building a chat system as a personal project to gain hands-on experience with Kafka and Hexagonal Architecture.

item.title: Ad Fallback Server Design Retrospective
item.description: Designing a Nest.js-based fallback server while removing a legacy ad server. Why a horizontal layered architecture fit better than Nest.js’s default vertical module slicing for a single API with complex business logic.

item.title: Cache Refresh Optimization Retrospective
item.description: How I reduced network costs and enabled instance downscaling by switching from full cache refresh to incremental refresh for campaign configuration data.

item.title: Two-Layer Control Loop for Ad Budget Pacing — Retrospective
item.description: A retrospective on moving ad budget pacing from a fixed-rule scheme to a two-layer control loop — per-campaign learning sets the baseline, real-time correction absorbs drift.

item.title: rust-server
item.description: A record of implementing the multithreaded HTTP server from Rust Book Chapter 20, experiencing how ownership and concurrency safety are enforced at the type level.

item.title: SwapDo Startup Story
item.description: SwapDo, a deepfake-based face synthesis meme service. A record of five months as a developer and team lead in a startup team.

item.title: 55L(GGS) Startup Story
item.description: A startup born from a casual League of Legends habit. From architecture design to desktop apps, a record of two people building a service that grew to 10,000 users over five months.

item.title: GDG Korea Android 11 Hackathon — YouTube Together
item.description: Entering the GDG Korea Android 11 Hackathon solo, building both server and app in three weeks.

item.title: KRIC Station Public Data Hackathon — Hidden Rest Areas
item.description: Korea Railroad Industry Information Center’s public-data hackathon. A three-person team built an Android app that surfaces hidden rest spaces inside subway stations, over three weeks.
